HAPPY SATURDAY, LEADERS!Apply to join us and other nonprofit leaders, funders, and social innovators at the Google.org Changemakers Forum in Washington, DC, on September 15.

 FFWD RESOURCES: FUNDER DATABASE, AI FOR HUMANITY RESOURCES HUB, AI GRANT WRITING COACH FUNDING & OPPORTUNITIES[Global] Stanley 1913: Creators Fund: Seeks early-stage organizations focused on mental health, sustainability, and community. Selected organizations receive $50K. Apply by September 13.[Global] Cisco Foundation: Global Impact Cash Grants: Invites organizations with tech-enabled programs in crisis response, education, economic empowerment, and climate resilience to submit a brief Letter of Inquiry. First-time recipients can request up to $100K. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.[Global] W.K. Kellogg Foundation: Supports innovative, community-driven organizations working on early childhood education, health equity, food systems, and economic security. Concentrated giving in Michigan, Mississippi, New Mexico, and New Orleans, with funding across the broader U.S., Mexico, and Haiti. Submit a Letter of Inquiry through the Fluxx portal at any time. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.[U.S.] Third Plateau: Resilient Organizations Learning Cohort: Seeks executive directors of gender-focused organizations into a free 10-week capacity-building cohort covering fundraising, governance, leadership, and organizational culture. Includes six virtual learning sessions and five 1:1 coaching sessions with Third Plateau strategists. Eligible organizations have annual budgets between $750K and $3M and 3 to 15 FTE. Apply by August 21.[U.S.] 92NY Belfer Center: UpTide Nonprofit Accelerator: Supports executive directors of community-building nonprofits with a $5K grant, personalized coaching, and a customized growth strategy. Outstanding organizations may receive up to $25K in additional funding at the final showcase. Apply by August 31.[U.S.] Smart Family Fund: Funds early-stage organizations with the potential for scalable impact that have not yet demonstrated the efficacy needed for growth funding. Awards first-time grants between $25K and $100K. Applications accepted on a rolling basis.[Southern U.S.] Mary Reynolds Babcock Foundation: Supports nonprofits working to move people and places out of poverty toward greater social and economic justice. Offers general operating support grants ranging from $10K to $100K. Applications accepted on a rolling basis. UPCOMING DEADLINES       Submit concept note by August 12 - [U.S.] GitLab Foundation: Powering Economic Opportunity Fund: Supports organizations that partner directly with employers, unions, and industry to strengthen work-based learning and improve job quality. Selected organizations receive up to $500K. Apply by August 12. Apply by August 14 - [U.S.] Civic Health Project AI for Civic Cohesion Fellowship: Seeks 5 early-stage teams building AI-powered tools to reduce polarization, improve civil discourse, and advance civic cohesion. Open to nonprofits, academic teams, and individual innovators with a working tool built in the last two years. Fellows also receive cohort access, a $10K grant, thought partnership with civic AI practitioners, and a pitch to a curated group of funders. Submit concept note by August 14.Apply by August 19 - [Global] iF Social Impact Prize: Seeks established projects working toward the UN Sustainable Development Goals with a design component. €100K is distributed across selected winners. Apply by August 19.  REMARKABLE EVENT[D.C.] Google.org DC Changemakers Forum: Brings together influential social innovators & nonprofits, philanthropic funders, academic pioneers, and agency heads to learn and discuss the pathways to scaled, ethical, socially impactful AI adoption and skilling. Google.org reviews and accepts applicants on a rolling basis until the September 15 event in DC. More info here.
